eligibility_reason: The adopted primary is the original familiar/unfamiliar encoding-axis geometry centered on Figure 2b,c, with source-defined regional/temporal comparisons and necessary controls. Five qualitative source summaries and one conflicting onset summary are a partial inventory only. Complete numerical outputs, source identities/reductions, computation verification and agreement criteria remain unresolved. Supporting feature decoding and other decoder alternatives do not replace this primary. Unchanged secondary improvement wording prevents final mixed-bundle binding.

source_paper.title: Temporal multiplexing of perception and memory codes in IT cortex

evidence.locator: An axis code for unfamiliar faces; Figure 2b,c and caption; coding-axis methods
evidence.supports: The registered result is time-dependent familiar/unfamiliar face-axis geometry in AM, PR and TP. Figure 2d,e contains separate face decoding, which is not the registered axis-geometry endpoint.

evidence.locator: Version 1; data and code archive description
evidence.supports: Author release contains responses to screening images and 1,000 monkey faces, feature coordinates and MATLAB coding-axis analysis. The 116.3-MB archive was not downloaded in this review.

Current six-curve reconstruction uses full-feature RMS scaling, 50-unit archive windows, a new fixed NumPy PCG64 sample realization and a TP-specific matched comparison; it explicitly disclaims biological improvement.

evidence.locator: Supplementary Methods: Preferred axis of cells; significance/consistency of axis tuning; matching face feature distributions; feature sensitivity; simple nonlinear model; additional Figure 2b,c legends
evidence.supports: Defines response-centered STA, whitened-STA control, first ten shape plus ten appearance coordinates, source-specific 964/36 comparisons, stimulus-set-specific sampling/repetition matching and 50-ms geometry windows at 10-ms steps. Does not supply a benchmark tolerance or immutable source identity joins.

evidence.locator: Results on familiar/unfamiliar axes, Figure 2b,c and caption; Extended Data 9a-c; tuning and reliability controls in Extended Data 3; matching diagnostics in Extended Data 8
evidence.supports: Reports higher unfamiliar-unfamiliar than unfamiliar-familiar axis similarity in AM/PR but not TP for the Figure 2b aggregate; AM/PR initially similar and later divergent time courses. The Figure 2c caption reports a late TP difference and PR onset 175 ms while the body gives 155 ms. Full region/time outputs and controls cannot be replaced by these summaries.

evidence.locator: Figure 2d,e and Supplementary Methods: face feature decoding and reconstruction; separate Figure 3c and Extended Data Figure 10k alternatives
evidence.supports: Unfamiliar-trained feature decoding/reconstruction is genuine supporting empirical evidence. Its 999-training/1000-fold schedule and ten identity shuffles are decoder requirements, not the geometry sampling protocol. Familiarity and identity classification remain separately unselected empirical alternatives.

target.description: Original familiar/unfamiliar axis-geometry comparison across AM, PR and TP and time, centered on Figure 2b,c with its indispensable source controls; no whole-paper, raw-spike or automatic inactivation requirement.

dataset.description: Use the original measured face-patch responses and matching face-feature coordinates released in Zenodo 10460607 v1 for the Figure 2b,c geometry and necessary source comparisons. Exact release members and response/feature/control joins remain unbound. This bounded primary does not require raw-spike reconstruction, every released file, all intervention panels or a newly selected decoder task.

cohort.description: Retain all original AM, PR and TP geometry populations, stimulus sets and their animal/session/neuron identities. Figure 2c reports AM 134 cells, PR 72 cells and TP 197 cells; these counts describe that source panel but do not authenticate the original per-cell roster or the different controls. The five-macaque study context is not evidence that every population samples every animal independently.

split.description: Preserve the original geometry comparison: axes from 964 unfamiliar faces versus axes from 36 omitted unfamiliar or 36 familiar faces, with the source stimulus-set-specific realization. For stimulus set 2 (most AM/PR), the Figure 2b legend pools 100 random 36-unfamiliar subsamples; for stimulus set 3 (PR of monkey E and TP), it uses the 36 unfamiliar faces presented at the same high repetition count as familiar faces. Preserve the 30/30 feature-matched AM/PR control and the source 36/36 feature-matched TP condition. Exact face/draw/repetition identities and control-specific fits remain unresolved. Decoder LOOCV folds and its ten shuffles are not primary geometry requirements.

inputs.description: Primary fitting consumes the source measured neural responses, stimulus/time/region identities and the first ten shape plus ten appearance features for each exact familiar/unfamiliar/control face. Refit preferred axes from those observations. Published conclusions and aggregates are common allowed inputs; authentic per-cell fits and output provenance, not copied figures, must demonstrate computation. Exact source input joins remain unresolved.

preprocessing.description: The source STA centers each neuron response over the selected stimuli and multiplies by their 20 feature coordinates. The supplement describes the full response window [50,300] ms and 50-ms sliding windows at 10-ms steps; its whitened-STA/linear-regression control uses the source feature covariance. Recover the original feature scaling, complete time grid/window boundaries, repetition averaging, finite-value/rank rules and stimulus-set-specific selections. Do not silently adopt the local adapter full-feature RMS, PCG64 draw realization, TP-specific selection or its unverified 100-ms paper-window assertion.

metric.description: Figure 2b,c compares preferred-axis cosine similarities for unfamiliar-unfamiliar and unfamiliar-familiar fits, separately by source region, time and control. The full geometry distributions and temporal summaries are required. The split-half reliability control separately uses Pearson correlation between axis vectors. A local six-curve RMSE, decoding correlation/accuracy, reconstruction MSE or a significance onset alone does not replace the primary geometry finding.

aggregation.description: Recover source aggregation for every region/time/control, including per-cell axes and cosines, the stimulus-set-specific 100-subsample pooling or repetition-matched comparison, distributions, time-course mean/SEM and defined support. Keep AM, PR and TP distinct and retain every original time window. Source neuron summaries and significance tests are distinct from independent-animal uncertainty; overlapping windows, cells and random draws are not independent animals. The local adapter averaging order is not automatically the original paper reduction.

full_panel.description: Primary scope is the complete original familiar/unfamiliar encoding-axis geometry centered on Figure 2b,c across AM/PR/TP and time, with the source low-contrast gain comparison, feature-matching diagnostics/comparisons, tuned-cell and reliability checks, whitened-STA comparison, and feature-sensitivity/output-nonlinearity checks needed for the axis-change interpretation. Preserve original numerical distributions, complete curves, fit/face/cell/time identities, statistical support and uncertainties. The partial source statements below do not encode or replace these numerical outputs. Figure 2d,e decoding/reconstruction remains separately identified supporting evidence with its own unresolved inputs, folds and controls; Figure 3c familiarity and Extended Data 10k identity decoding remain distinct unselected alternatives. No automatic whole-paper, all-Extended-Data, raw-spike, ML-decoder or inactivation enrollment.

permitted_observations.description: Use the original measured response/feature observations needed to estimate the source geometry, preserving familiarity, contrast, stimulus-set and reliability-control identities. No new held-out face/animal split or invented secret-label regime is introduced. The paper and published geometry claims are visible inputs; independent verification must inspect a frozen data-dependent analysis and granular fitted outputs. Exact paired paper+data versus paper+data+official-code materials, exposure and resource protocol remain unqualified.

This deliberate primary/secondary difference must be reconciled by the canonical owner before a same-task outcome bundle can be bound; no outcomes file is authored or repaired here.
